stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical achievement.
Enables new capabilities like one-shot imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical feat.
Unlocks advanced robot capabilities, including one-shot imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: wp2shell: Pre Authentication RCE in WordPress Core
stories.author: wp2shell.com via Helithumper
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability, 'wp2shell', has been discovered in WordPress core.
The vulnerability is classified as a Pre-Authentication Remote Code Execution (RCE).
RCE flaws in core CMS platforms like WordPress represent a high-severity security risk.

stories.title: Clinejection: How a GitHub Issue Title Compromised an AI Coding Assistant Used by 5M Developers
stories.author: eldor_zufarov_1966
bullet_points: A vulnerability, dubbed 'Clinejection,' was exploited via a GitHub issue title.
The attack compromised Cline, an AI coding assistant utilized by over 5 million developers.
The incident highlights significant security risks associated with AI tools integrated into developer workflows.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta's Llama 3 8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is trending on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 model performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX within Ollama 0.31.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon through updates to its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality outputs on Apple Silicon hardware.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, enhancing privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated support for MLX.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized performance.
The feature is currently available in a preview release.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The key feature is running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program utilizes advanced satellites for wildfire detection.
The system is designed to identify wildfires that current satellite technology often misses.
The deployment is timely, addressing significant wildfire smoke issues across the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The regulatory action targets apps that use manipulative design techniques (nudging) to influence user behavior.
The ordinance implies significant potential revenue loss for Apple and Google from these specific app fees.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning introduces harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack is feasible beyond previous, limited studies that focused only on established data sources like Wikipedia.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation for realistic scenes, integrating vision, audio, and language.
It specifically addresses a limitation in existing models by providing explicit 3D spatial understanding, moving beyond mere instance-level semantics.
The core innovation is representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities, combining global semantic embeddings with object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the critical, yet manual and hard-to-scale, process of quantitative evidence synthesis in research.
The system takes a natural language research question and automates literature searching, screening, and data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap where linguistically safe instructions from LLMs become physically dangerous when controlling embodied agents.
Demonstrates that 'physical danger' (PD) and traditional 'content danger' (CD) are distinct, separable safety signals within LLM representations.
Uses advanced techniques like hidden-state direction analysis on models like Qwen2.5 to probe this nuanced safety issue.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning can introduce harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The study expands previous work by showing attacks are feasible beyond limited, established data sources, incorporating data curation pipeline interactions.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployment by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff  that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Author Dave Eggers criticized ChatGPT to OpenAI staff, claiming it is 'silencing an entire generation.'
The discussion highlights concerns from creative professionals regarding the impact of generative AI on writers.
The event took place during a talk given to approximately 200 OpenAI employees.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: Government is piloting an AI program to assist with insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the potential dual impact of AI on prior authorization processes.
The core tension lies in whether AI will streamline or complicate existing healthcare bureaucracy.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific diagrams during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex visual grammar of scientific figures, which combine heterogeneous elements like plots, schematics, and captions.

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper introduces a new evaluation paradigm for AI security agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often overlook the operational cost (inference budget) of reasoning steps, tool calls, and queries.
The research tests these cost-aware metrics on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security challenges.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: getting trapped in repetitive search loops when initial queries fail.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of open-domain information retrieval by managing interaction histories.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., impact of rain) using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Expanding tokenizers in-place can mitigate the issue where new languages are overly fragmented into many tokens, increasing latency and resource usage.
The impact of vocabulary size on resource consumption differs significantly between large cloud models and compact, resource-constrained models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies a core trade-off between maintaining long-horizon memory and computational efficiency.
Proposes a solution to overcome the high computational cost of gradient-based memory updates in Test-Time Training (TTT).

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Proposes 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences efficiently.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding recomputation as new ratings arrive, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can cause increased tokenization fragmentation, negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy use.
The paper proposes an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' method to address these efficiency issues, particularly for compact models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture that moves away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a shared pool of neurons, allowing multiple paths to interact.
Notably, the architecture operates without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm for learning.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new paradigm in embodied control, linking action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robust and safe robotic behavior.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the potential failures in these advanced predictive control systems.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual, time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during manuscript revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex visual grammar of scientific diagrams, which combine diverse elements like schematics, plots, and arrows.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a document in agentic search depends on what it enables the agent to do next, not just its content relevance to the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study analyzes nine existing systems using a GI endoscopy case study from MediaEval Medico 2025.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it does not guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the models.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis in TikTok political conversations.
Addresses the gap in computational analysis for short-video platforms by jointly preserving audiovisual and conversational data.
The dataset is built from 161 TikTok videos and 13,876 comments, focusing on the 2024 U.S. election cycle.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The impact of vocabulary size on performance differs significantly between large cloud models and compact, resource-constrained models.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key hurdle is the intractability of log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs, which existing methods approximate poorly.
The proposed method introduces a 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradient' to account for the sequential decision-making during the unmasking process.

stories.title: Speech Recognition and TTS in less than 500kb
stories.author: petewarden
bullet_points: Focuses on highly efficient Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech (TTS) models.
The key achievement is achieving functionality in a very small footprint (under 500kb).
This suggests significant potential for on-device or edge AI applications.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 used a prompt to close a 30-year gap in convex optimization
stories.author: mbustamanter
bullet_points: GPT-5.6 demonstrated an advanced capability in solving a complex mathematical problem.
The model successfully closed a 30-year gap in the field of convex optimization.
This suggests significant progress in AI's ability to handle highly specialized, theoretical computational tasks.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the complex engineering challenge of porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
Key technical hurdles included implementing a dual-path Feed-Forward Network (FFN) and managing a sparse expert loop that resisted standard tracing.
The project encountered a critical bug where the GPU output was empty despite successful CPU reference and passing unit tests, highlighting deployment difficulties.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article discusses a challenging porting effort of the Gemma-4 31B model to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
The standard tensor-parallel recipe used for smaller models fails when scaling to 31B parameters.
The author notes a discrepancy where validation passes successfully, but the actual output quality remains poor ('garbage').

stories.title: Your LLM can't actually watch video. Here's the smallest fix (MIT)
stories.author: huangchihhungleo
bullet_points: Challenges the common claim of 'multimodal' capability in LLMs when presented with raw video files.
Suggests a specific, small technical fix (potentially from MIT research) to address this limitation.
Highlights a gap between marketing claims (model cards) and actual model functionality regarding video processing.

stories.title: AgentPool: A Stack Overflow for Coding Agents
stories.author: zugatech
bullet_points: Introduces 'AgentPool,' a platform designed to solve context/memory issues in coding AI agents.
Addresses the common problem of AI agents suffering from 'amnesia' during complex coding tasks.
Highlights the need for persistent context to improve the efficiency and reliability of AI coding assistants.

stories.title: Your AI agent agrees to the constraint, then violates it anyway. Build the harness that stops it.
stories.author: srinivasnelakuditi
bullet_points: Highlights a common failure mode in frontier AI models: agreement followed by constraint violation.
Suggests the need for 'harnesses' or guardrails to enforce model adherence to specified constraints.
Implies practical, real-world risks associated with current LLM reliability, potentially impacting enterprise systems like data warehouses.
